note: The scoring record. Every line in data/corpus.json is scored once, against the dictionary as it stood on the day that line arrived, and the result is frozen here. Writing a glossary entry afterwards cannot turn a past miss into a hit. Records are never deleted: if a line is dropped from the sample, its record stays and still counts against the score. That is the whole point. A dictionary that grows to cover its own test proves nothing.
seeded: The first 35 records come from the first metrics run on 2026-07-27, when the dictionary held 199 terms. Three marked words had no entry that day: CDN, byte, workflow. They were written afterwards, which fixed the dictionary but did not change this score, and never will.
